question: What will Drewry's Shanghai–Los Angeles container freight rate be in the October 1, 2026 World Container Index release?

calls.reasoning: Anchor is the Sep 17, 2026 print of $7,712 with two assessments to go (Sep 24, then the resolving Oct 1 one). Reference class - the first WCI Shanghai-LA print on/after Oct 1 versus the mid-September print two weeks earlier, 2021-2025 - is mildly negative (median about -4%; Oct 3, 2025 was -5% w/w to $2,196; 2024 was drifting down 1-3%/wk into October), because the pre-holiday rush peaks in mid-September. Adjusting up from that base: 2026 has strong positive momentum (five consecutive increases, +23% in a month), Drewry itself guides to a further rise for Sep 24, 9 transpacific blank sailings are booked, Shanghai berth waits rose 65->78 hrs, carriers have run ~17 rate increases this year versus ~6 normally, and cargo shipped in late Sept/early Oct is the last that lands before the Nov 10 truce expiry. Adjusting down: Mid-Autumn (Sep 25-27) plus Golden Week (Oct 1-7) puts the resolving week inside the demand lull, Asia-Europe is already falling 5-9%/wk, peak season is reported as closing early, and a likely truce extension at the Sep 24 Trump-Xi summit removes front-loading urgency. Net: roughly flat-to-slightly-up from a Sep 24 print I expect near $7,900-8,000, so a median around $7,900 with wide, near-symmetric-in-log bands. No human market prices this; evidence on the Oct 1 week specifically is thin, so I stay close to the momentum-adjusted anchor rather than betting on a turn.

BASE RATES / HISTORY: (a) over the five Golden-Week-week prints 2021-2025, the first WCI Shanghai-LA assessment on/after Oct 1 came in below the mid-September print two weeks earlier in most years - 2025: Oct 3 print $2,196, -5% w/w, composite $1,669 -5% (FreshPlaza/Drewry); 2024: mid-Oct print $5,019 with the lane drifting -1% to -3%/wk through Sept-Oct; 2022 was a collapse regime (double-digit weekly declines); 2021 was a high plateau with small declines. (b) Conditional on entering late September with rising momentum (as in 2026) rather than falling momentum, that class has few observations - 2024 and 2025 both entered September declining, so the unconditional seasonal figure is computed over a differently-conditioned set. (c) 2026 weekly changes on this lane have ranged about -2% to +10%; 2025 on the same lane saw far larger shock weeks (+40%-plus and -20%-plus) during tariff whiplash, so the 1-2 year 10-90 band of 2-week changes is materially wider than the 2026-only band. (d) Year-over-year the lane is up about 201% (BofA graphic cited by Zero Hedge, 2026-09-20); Asia-USWC was $1,963/FEU in mid-December 2025 (Freightos/FreightWaves).

SUPPLY/CAPACITY: 9 transpacific blank sailings announced for the week after Sep 17, up from 8 the prior week and 6 the week before (Drewry Container Capacity Insight); Asia-Europe blanks rose from 1 to 4. Alliances reported cancelling 18-25% of scheduled Asia-Europe and transpacific sailings across the Mid-Autumn/Golden Week window; MSC blanked its Asia-USEC Emerald service in week 41 citing the anticipated slowdown during and after Golden Week (Loadstar). Shanghai berth waiting time 65 hrs (week 36) -> 78 hrs (week 37); earlier in the season typhoons (incl. Typhoon Saudel) closed Shanghai and Ningbo for days, with reports of ~90 vessels waiting and >1.5m containers stuck at Shanghai/Ningbo anchorages (Freightos, Sept 2026). Ships are returning to the Suez routing (Premier Alliance members plus a Cosco-group OOCL vessel eastbound), which shortens Asia-Europe voyages and releases effective tonnage; Houthi statements about targeting Saudi-linked ships keep the Red Sea routing unsettled (Al-Mal citing Drewry/Linerlytica, 2026-09-20). Freight Right reports vessel schedules deteriorating, with rollovers plus delays reaching nearly two weeks.

DEMAND / CALENDAR / POLICY: China Mid-Autumn Festival 25-27 Sept and National Day Golden Week 1-7 Oct, with only three working days between them and make-up working days on 20 Sept and 10 Oct. NRF projected US ocean import volumes broadly flat in September then declining in October. Freight Right headlined peak season as nearing an early close (wk of 2026-09-07). Carriers have pushed roughly 17 rate increases on East Asia-USA this year versus about 6 in a normal year, with the Sept 1 GRI implemented on both coasts and a Sept 15 round anticipated; Drewry's stated expectation in the Sep 17 release is for transpacific rates to rise slightly the following week on pre-Golden-Week demand and continued capacity management, and for Asia-Europe to decline slightly. US-China: one-year truce expires 2026-11-10; Xi visits Washington 23-25 Sept with a Trump meeting on 24 Sept; analysts describe a one-year extension of the Busan truce as the most likely deliverable, with rare-earth and AI-export-control disputes the main breakdown risk; the US was reported planning a 7.5% China overcapacity tariff around the summit, and separately reported on 18 Sept to have delayed some China tariffs. Cargo loaded in late September/early October is the last that arrives in the US before the 10 Nov expiry. Panama Canal low-water surcharges were flagged as a possible USEC-specific pressure. Applied US tariff rate reported at a record 11.7-12.5% covering 54% of goods imports.

calls.reconciliation: Four factual disputes. (1) Aug 20 level $6,802 vs $6,272 - unsettleable without retrieval, and immaterial since all runs agree the 17 Sep anchor is $7,712 with two prints remaining. (2) Reference-class direction: Run 1's negative seasonal rests entirely on 2024 and 2025, both cited in the dossiers as mid-downtrend years (Oct 2025 was the 16th straight composite decline), while Run 2's flat-to-positive entries are rising-regime years - so the disagreement dissolves: the negative is trend, not season, and 2026 is a rising regime. Prior taken as flat-to-modestly-positive, ~$7,800. (3) All three runs searched for a 1 Oct GRI and none found one; Freightos 15 Sep says most carriers had not announced October increases. Settled as absent - upside optionality only. (4) Run 3's FBX01 futures at ~$6,825 vs spot ~$7,600: checked against the contract terms and it settles on a MONTHLY AVERAGE of a different index and lane composite, so an October average below late-September spot is consistent with a peak on/around 1 Oct followed by a fade - it is not a bear signal for this specific print, and I decline to treat it as an anchor. The remaining dispute (does the 1 Oct print catch the rush or the vacuum) is pure judgment; the assessment week covers the 28-30 Sep compressed loading window and both Drewry's and Xeneta's dated forward statements point at the rush, so I take that side. I land marginally above where the runs clustered, and materially wider than all of them: their dispersion came from the last five calm weeks, whereas this lane's own 2025-26 history includes +20% and -15% weeks, which is the width I price.
